description: Representative Mike Levin (CA-49) seeks Staff Assistant for his DC office. This position is responsible for managing the front desk, answering the DC office phones, operating the DC office internship program, coordinating constituents' tour and flag requests, planning and drafting basic correspondence, and handling additional administrative duties of the office as assigned. The staff member in this role interacts regularly with constituents and should have a friendly, helpful demeanor. The ideal candidate should have strong written and verbal communications skills, extreme attention to detail, and a positive attitude. A working knowledge of legislative process and major policy issues is a plus. This staff member should also be a self-starter who likes to solve problems and works well with a team. Strong organizational skills and a passion for helping others are essential to this role. Possession of a driver's license, a clean driving record, and a personal vehicle are preferred in order to drive the Member in DC. Driving responsibilities could include frequent short distances during days that the House is in session and some driving in the evening. Salary range is $45,000-$50,000, commensurate with experience. Start date for the position is September 21, 2026.
responsibilities: Managing the front desk
Answering the DC office phones
Operating the DC office internship program
Coordinating constituents' tour and flag requests
Planning and drafting basic correspondence
Handling additional administrative duties of the office as assigned
Driving the Member in DC, including frequent short distances during days that the House is in session and some driving in the evening
qualifications: Friendly, helpful demeanor
Strong written and verbal communications skills
Extreme attention to detail
Positive attitude
Working knowledge of legislative process and major policy issues is a plus
Self-starter who likes to solve problems and works well with a team
Strong organizational skills
Passion for helping others
Possession of a driver's license, a clean driving record, and a personal vehicle are preferred
how_to_apply: Send a resume, cover letter, two writing samples, and a list of three references to ca49.applications@mail.house.gov with "Staff Assistant" in the subject line. Send all materials in one PDF document and indicate personal vehicle access in the body of the email. Incomplete applications will not be considered.
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer; we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, gender identity or expression, or sexual orientation. We deeply value the diversity of our employees and encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply.

description: The Office of Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29) is seeking a detail-oriented, energetic, and reliable District Scheduler/Staff Assistant based in the San Fernando Valley in a full-time, in-person capacity. This position is responsible for the Member's Schedule in the District, as well as maintaining front office and administrative operations for the District Office. This position works closely with the Member, Chief of Staff, District Director, and DC Scheduler on all scheduling activities in the District, as well as assisting District Office Staff as needed. The position requires flexibility to work long hours, including nights and weekends. Diverse and bilingual candidates are encouraged to apply. The annual salary range is $55,000 - $58,000 depending on experience. There is a standard package of federal benefits. Plus, a Student Loan Repayment Program is provided.
responsibilities: Organizing and tracking scheduling requests and speaking engagements and responding in a timely and friendly manner
Compiling the Member's daily briefing materials during District Work Period
Record-keeping of the Member's attendance for various District events and coverage in areas in the District
Assisting with District projects such as the Congressional Art Competition
Answering phones, monitoring constituent requests, greeting visitors
Maintaining reception area and conference room
Ordering office supplies
Drafting and printing District specific correspondence
Additional duties as assigned
qualifications: Time management and multitasking skills
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment
Excellent written and oral communications skills
Sound decision-making and good judgment
Friendly and professional demeanor
Ability to exercise discretion
Flexibility to work long hours, including nights and weekends
Customer Service and Administrative experience are a plus
how_to_apply: Interested candidates are encouraged to submit a cover letter, resume, and writing sample in one PDF to ca29jobs@gmail.com with the following subject line: "District Scheduler/Staff Assistant - [candidate's full name]".
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, sex (including marital or parental status), color, age, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, or disability.

description: The Front Office Supervisor supervises a team of three Front Office Assistants who provide essential administrative and clerical support services to the staff within the House Office of the Legislative Counsel (HOLC). The Front Office Supervisor oversees the operations of the Front Office and communicates with Office management regarding the operation and performance of the Front Office. The Front Office Supervisor may work on special projects at the request and under the direction of the Legislative Counsel. After an initial 90-day period, the Front Office Supervisor is eligible to telework up to one day per week, at the discretion of the Legislative Counsel.
responsibilities: Supervises a team of three Front Office Assistants.
Ensures the effective day-to-day operations of the Front Office.
Develops and maintains general working knowledge and understanding of HOLC's practices and the legislative process.

Serves as a primary representative of HOLC by providing friendly, professional, and helpful customer service to office visitors and callers, including by addressing general and routine inquiries and forwarding messages as appropriate.

Ensures that the Front Office has adequate in-office presence and phone coverage during official business hours and after hours, as necessary, including by coordinating the schedules of the Front Office Assistants.
Carefully assesses and distributes client requests to attorneys and paralegals by phone and email.
Ensures the work of the Front Office team is performed accurately and consistently.
Maintains the HOLC general inbox and ensures prompt and accurate HOLC correspondence with internal and external individuals.
Maintains the schedule for Front Office staff and keeps accurate and up to date the schedule and leave records of all HOLC staff.
Coordinates miscellaneous general office services, including ordering office furnishings, materials, and supplies, and maintains the office legal library.
Coordinates requests and projects on behalf of the Office that involve communication with other House offices.
qualifications: A bachelor's degree or a combination of education and relevant work experience, including some supervisory or management experience.
Must be a United States citizen.
Professional background cannot contain partisan political work.
Ability to maintain decorum in high stress situations and exhibit a high standard of customer service.
Ability to provide administrative support, including assessing and disseminating requests, scheduling meetings, and managing records.
Ability to provide friendly, professional, and helpful customer service.
Ability to switch rapidly between multiple tasks during busy periods while maintaining a strong attention to detail.
Knowledge of, and ability to use, various automated office systems and software programs, including record management systems, Microsoft Office, and Adobe Acrobat.
Ability to analyze problems and recommend appropriate solutions or changes.
Ability to establish effective working relationships with HOLC staff, office management, and clients.
Ability to work autonomously and within a team.
Ability to handle sensitive and confidential matters with tact and maintain impartiality in judgment and in action.
Ability to communicate, orally and in writing, in a professional and effective manner with clients, colleagues, and other people.
how_to_apply: Qualified candidates please submit your cover letter and resume by August 12th via this link.
equal_opportunity: All applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, sex (including marital or parental status), disability, or age.

This role reports to the Communications Director and works closely with the Digital Manager. This is an ideal opportunity for someone who is excited to learn and passionate about new and traditional storytelling.
responsibilities: Draft written materials, including speeches, releases, quotes, video scripts, social media posts, and e-newsletters.
Monitor local and national news, and social media; manage daily press clips; maintain press lists.
Assist with franked communications strategy, including creating digital ads.
Manage website and digital archives.
Staff Member at DC-based events; take photos and videos.
Other duties as assigned.
qualifications: Spanish language proficiency is strongly preferred.
Ability to work occasional nights and weekends.
Entry-level and experienced candidates are both encouraged to apply.

description: The Communications and Correspondence Assistant supports district-based efforts to communicate and liaise with stakeholders and key audiences in person and across platforms. The Communications and Correspondence Assistant manages the Congresswoman's district communications with constituents. They build out coordinated outreach and comms plans that leverage opportunities to highlight local leaders/networks in the district, increase commendations, convene and connect, create press and social media pop moments, maximize Office visibility, and build the opt-in list. The position is based in-district. Regular travel between Chicago and DuPage County will be required. The ideal candidate is a team player who can juggle multiple projects, deliver high-quality, professional work quickly under high pressure and with tight deadlines, develop and implement new ideas, take and implement feedback effectively, and stay organized. The position assumes flexible hours, including long hours, nights, and weekends, as needed.
responsibilities: Implement the Office's aligned comms and outreach plan and strategy, representing the Congresswoman in the field
Support the Office's bilingual (SPAN/ENG) digital strategy and website maintenance in collaboration with the Communications Director
Assist in the execution of the Office's media and public relations strategy for the Member
Support the execution of press conferences, tele-town halls, and other events in both Washington, D.C., and the District
Coordinate across functions to advance strategic priorities
Performs other duties as assigned
qualifications: 1-2 years of experience in field or communications for elected officials, government agencies, non-profit organizations, or similar entities
Fluency in Spanish is highly preferred
Strong ability to build relationships with a broad range of government and community stakeholders
Strong writing, editing, and proofreading skills with a track record of action-oriented/persuasive writing yielding results
Strong understanding of print, broadcast, and online media
Functional understanding of Canva, Adobe Pro, and other platforms for communication, design and engagement
Ability to build and maintain positive working relationships and to coordinate efforts to reduce silos; willingness to accept direction and performance-based criticism in stride, adapt, and deliver

Capable of producing high-quality communications materials quickly, under tight deadlines with limited support; track record of exceptional planning and time management; ability to work under pressure and comfortable balancing multiple responsibilities at once
Politically savvy and skilled at navigating challenging situations with constituents, the press and staff

description: Representative Raúl Ruiz, M.D. is a Senior Member of the Energy and Commerce Committee and former Chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus. The Office of Representative Ruiz seeks a Legislative Assistant to lead a portfolio focused on health policy and other issues as assigned in his Washington, D.C. office. The Legislative Assistant will support the Congressman's work on the Energy and Commerce Committee's Subcommittee on Health. This is not an entry-level position. Salary is commensurate with experience; the office offers competitive and comprehensive benefits. The Legislative Assistant will work closely with the Legislative Director and Chief of Staff to develop and execute a coordinated legislative strategy across health and assigned issue areas. The ideal candidate is highly motivated, detail-oriented, and able to work under pressure while meeting deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Candidates with ties to California are encouraged to apply.
responsibilities: Lead the Congressman's legislative portfolio on health policy and other assigned issue areas.
Support the Congressman's work on the Energy and Commerce Committee's Subcommittee on Health, including preparing for and staffing committee hearings and markups.
Work with the Legislative Director and Chief of Staff to develop and execute a coordinated health care legislative strategy.
Draft legislation, amendments, and cosponsor recruitment materials.
Write talking points, briefing materials, and memoranda pertaining to assigned issue areas.
Monitor policy developments across the assigned portfolio and proactively flag emerging issues for leadership.
Work closely with the communications and district teams to advance the Congressman's health policy priorities.
Interact with key constituent groups and stakeholders, including patient advocates, health care providers, insurers, and federal agency officials.
Perform additional duties as assigned by the Legislative Director and Chief of Staff.
qualifications: A bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant experience.
Either 2–3 years of Capitol Hill experience or relevant health policy experience.
Strong written and oral communication skills, including demonstrated ability to draft legislation, amendments, talking points, briefing materials, and memoranda.
Familiarity with the congressional committee process, including preparation for and staffing of hearings and markups.
Knowledge of federal health policy, including issues within the jurisdiction of the Energy and Commerce Committee's Subcommittee on Health.
Demonstrated ability to manage a legislative portfolio and develop proactive policy strategy in coordination with leadership staff.
Ability to work collaboratively with communications and district teams and to engage effectively with constituent groups, advocacy organizations, and agency officials.
Strong attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
California ties are a plus.
how_to_apply: All interested candidates are encouraged to submit a resume and cover letter with "Legislative Assistant: Last Name" as the subject line to CA25resumes@mail.house.gov
